title: Scale Technique and Finger Independence — MusicXML Exercises

source.instructionsOrigin: User-provided revised instructions in the conversation
source.precedence: The revised sourceInstructions in this JSON supersede the original Word document. The document name and SHA-256 identify the original reference only.

sourceInstructions: All generated exercises must follow the original key signature and use 4/4 time. Write all moving notes as eighth notes, except when eighth-note triplets are required. Preserve the original pitches and fingerings when possible. Each exercise must appear on a separate musical line. If scale passages occur in both hands, generate the exercises separately for each hand. Display finger numbers in the score. For exercises involving a held finger, use two simultaneous MusicXML voices: one for the moving notes and another for the sustained note, tied continuously without repeated attacks.

methods.title: Fourth-Finger High Lift

applicability.description: A selected scale passage involving the fourth finger.

measures.directionAboveStaff: Lift finger 4 higher than usual before playing.

methods.directionAboveExercise: Lift finger 4 higher than usual before playing.
sourceInstructions: If the selected measure contains a scale passage involving finger 4, generate two measures using the original sequence of notes.
In Measure 1, add accents to every note played by finger 4. Above the staff, write: "Lift finger 4 higher than usual before playing."
In Measure 2, repeat the same sequence without accents and add: "Return to natural finger movement."
Write eight eighth notes per measure. If the original passage contains fewer than eight notes, repeat the sequence. If it contains more than eight, use the first eight.

methods.title: Fourth-Finger Release and Retention

applicability.description: Selected notes played by the fourth finger.

measures.movement: Release the key immediately after playing.
Hold the key for its full written duration before releasing.

sourceInstructions: If the selected measure contains notes played by finger 4, generate two measures using the original note sequence.
In Measure 1, apply staccato to every note played by finger 4, indicating immediate release after striking the key.
In Measure 2, apply tenuto to the same notes, indicating that finger 4 must remain on the key for its full written duration.
Keep all other notes unchanged. Write eight eighth notes per measure, repeating or shortening the original sequence as necessary.

methods.title: Holding Finger 5 While Fingers 3 and 4 Move

applicability.description: Three adjacent scale notes assigned to fingers three, four and five.

movingVoice.pitchDerivation: If necessary, derive three adjacent scale notes from the original key signature.

methods.directionAboveExercise: Hold finger 5 while alternating fingers 3 and 4.
sourceInstructions: This is a one-hand exercise. If the selected measure contains scale passages in both hands, generate the exercise separately for each hand.
Generate two measures using three adjacent scale notes assigned to fingers 3, 4 and 5. If necessary, derive these notes from the original key signature.
Finger 5 must remain continuously depressed while fingers 3 and 4 alternate.
Use the following moving-finger pattern in both measures: 3–4–3–4–3–4–3–4.
In Measure 1, accent every note played by finger 3. In Measure 2, accent every note played by finger 4.

Write eight moving eighth notes per measure in Voice 1. Write the sustained note played by finger 5 in Voice 2, using tied eighth notes across both measures. Both voices must sound simultaneously. Finger 5 must be attacked only once at the beginning of the exercise.
At the top, write: "Hold finger 5 while alternating fingers 3 and 4."

methods.title: Holding Finger 3 While Fingers 1, 2, 4 and 5 Move

applicability.description: Always generate for a selected scale passage, even when the original measure does not contain all five fingerings.

methods.directionAboveExercise: Hold finger 3 continuously while playing with fingers 1, 2, 4 and 5.
sourceInstructions: This is a one-hand exercise. If the selected measure contains scale passages in both hands, generate the exercise separately for each hand.
Always generate this exercise for a selected scale passage, even if the original measure does not contain all five fingerings.
Generate two measures using five consecutive scale notes in the original key. Assign fingers 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 according to the natural five-finger position of the selected hand.
Finger 3 must hold its assigned note continuously throughout both measures. Fingers 1, 2, 4 and 5 must independently play the remaining four notes without releasing or repeating the held note.
In Measure 1, use the finger pattern: 1–2–4–5–4–2–1–2.
In Measure 2, use the finger pattern: 5–4–2–1–2–4–5–4.
For example, in C major with the right hand, assign C4–D4–E4–F4–G4 to fingers 1–2–3–4–5. Hold E4 with finger 3.
Measure 1: C4–D4–F4–G4–F4–D4–C4–D4.
Measure 2: G4–F4–D4–C4–D4–F4–G4–F4.
For the left hand, reverse the natural finger assignment: C3–D3–E3–F3–G3 correspond to fingers 5–4–3–2–1. Hold E3 with finger 3 and apply the same finger patterns.

MusicXML requirements: Voice 1 must contain eight moving eighth notes per measure. Voice 2 must contain the sustained third-finger note, written as tied eighth notes across both measures. Both voices must sound simultaneously. The sustained note must be attacked only once and must never appear in the moving-note sequence.
At the top, write: "Hold finger 3 continuously while playing with fingers 1, 2, 4 and 5."

methods.title: Triplet Accent Shifting With Finger 5 Held

applicability.description: A suitable scale passage using adjacent notes assigned to fingers three, four and five.

methods.directionAboveExercise: Hold finger 5 and shift the accents between the moving fingers.
sourceInstructions: This is a one-hand exercise. If the selected measure contains scale passages in both hands, generate the exercise separately for each hand.
Generate three measures using three adjacent scale notes assigned to fingers 3, 4 and 5.
Hold finger 5 continuously while fingers 3 and 4 alternate in four eighth-note triplets per measure.
Use this moving-finger pattern in all three measures: 3–4–3 | 4–3–4 | 3–4–3 | 4–3–4.
In Measure 1, accent the first note of each triplet. In Measure 2, accent the second note of each triplet. In Measure 3, accent the third note of each triplet.

Voice 1 must contain twelve eighth-note triplets per measure, notated as four groups of three notes in the time of two eighth notes. Voice 2 must contain the sustained fifth-finger note, tied continuously across all three measures without repeated attacks.
At the top, write: "Hold finger 5 and shift the accents between the moving fingers."

methods.title: Repeated Three-Finger Scale Patterns

applicability.description: A scale-like passage involving fingers three, four and five.

methods.directionAboveExercise: Play each pattern as fast and accurately as possible while maintaining relaxed finger movements.
sourceInstructions: This is a one-hand exercise for improving the coordination and independence of fingers 3, 4 and 5. If the selected measure contains scale passages in both hands, generate the exercise separately for each hand.

Generate two measures using three adjacent scale notes assigned to fingers 3, 4 and 5. If the selected passage contains fewer than three suitable notes, extend the pattern using the original key signature.
In Measure 1, use the finger pattern: 3–4–5–4–3–4–5–4.
In Measure 2, use the finger pattern: 5–4–3–4–5–4–3–4.
Write eight eighth notes per measure. Accent every note played by finger 4 in both measures. Use the same three pitches throughout the exercise.
At the top, write: "Play each pattern as fast and accurately as possible while maintaining relaxed finger movements."

implementationNotes.origin: Application integration notes, separate from the revised user instructions.
implementationNotes.methodSelection: The instructions define six methods. Exercise 4 must always be generated for a selected scale passage; the overall number of other methods selected per request is unspecified.
implementationNotes.fingeringEvidence: Preserve original pitches and fingerings when possible and display assigned finger numbers. For methods 3, 4 and 6, follow their explicit key-based pitch derivation rules. Do not reject Exercise 4 because source fingerings are incomplete. Required source fingerings and assigned exercise fingers are distinct.
implementationNotes.heldNoteDurations: Exercises 3 and 4 require eight tied eighth notes in Voice 2 per measure, with ties continuing across both measures. Exercise 5 requires a continuous tied Voice 2 across all three measures but does not specify the written values of its held-note segments. The two voices occupy the same time, not consecutive time.
unspecifiedDetails: No numeric tempo marking is specified.
The exact written note values for the sustained voice in Exercise 5 are not specified.
rendererRequirements: Independent simultaneous voices with ties for held notes
implementationNotes.backendIntegration: Czerny No. 1 uses the dedicated czerny1-practice generator. The AI receives these rules and the detected passage to write analysis; the backend generates and validates the exercise notation. Each response contains two separate exercises, with Exercise 4 first for each detected hand. Further requests use unused methods; exhaustion returns an error while retaining existing exercises.
